chunks: From him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in the matter of
a man who has sexual intercourse with his wife after he has contracted the Ihram but has not yet recited the Talbiyah, he said: There is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: The specific recitation of 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' marking the formal start of Hajr rituals
key_terms.شَيْء: Thing, here implying a penalty, fine, or expiation (daman/kaffarah)
key_terms.يَقَعُ: To have sexual intercourse (specifically in the context of marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim has sex with his wife after entering Ihram but before saying Talbiyah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani highlights the precise temporal boundary of Ihram obligations, distinguishing between the contractual entry (I'qad) and the vocal declaration (Talbiyah). In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is crucial for determining whether minor infractions incur immediate penalties or are excused, reflecting the Imams' attention to ritual precision. The ruling underscores that the state of Ihram is fully operative for prohibitions like sexual intercourse only after the Talbiyah is recited, aligning with the principle that ritual status follows the complete act of consecration.
